name: Canyon Floor Inflow Terrace
why_habitability: The southern terrace of the canyon floor where the fluvial feature originates. Exposed bedrock here preserves the basal transition into the stream deposit. Studying these lower strata can determine the initial hydraulic energy and water chemistry of the channel system.
notes: Southern reach of the canyon floor channel in HiRISE PSP_006855_1750.

name: Inverted Fluvial Channel Crest
why_habitability: A prominent sinuous positive-relief ridge interpreted as an inverted riverbed. Stream sediments became cemented in place by water-deposited minerals before surrounding softer terrain was eroded by wind. This provides direct morphological evidence of past sustained liquid water flow.
notes: Explicitly described as an inverted channel deposit on the HiRISE observation page.

name: East Wall Stratified Outcrop
why_habitability: Finely layered sedimentary bedrock exposed on the lower slopes of the eastern canyon wall. These rhythmic strata record fluctuating water levels and sediment deposition in an ancient lacustrine or groundwater-fed environment. Astronauts can sample across sequential layers to reconstruct climate history.
notes: Stereo observation PSP_007501_1750 documenting canyon wall layering.

name: Sinuous Debris Levee Margin
why_habitability: Distinct lateral levees and debris flow margins preserved along the inner canyon floor. Geomorphological modeling demonstrates that mobilizing this coarse material on low slopes required pore water saturation and groundwater exfiltration. It provides evidence for late-stage aqueous mass transport.
notes: Details groundwater-assisted mass movements and levees in this canyon.

name: Polyhydrated Sulfate Splay
why_habitability: Terminal debris deposit exhibiting strong orbital spectral signatures of polyhydrated sulfates. Solute transport and evaporation of Mg-rich pore waters likely cemented these deposits, creating high preservation potential for chemical biosignatures. The low-slope terrain makes it safe for surface sampling.
notes: Documents polyhydrated sulfate signatures and canyon floor debris deposits.
